body.question: Which is bigger: the number of trees on Earth, or the number of stars in the Milky Way?
body.reveal: A global survey estimated about 3.04 trillion trees on Earth. The Milky Way holds roughly 100 to 400 billion stars, so there are around ten times more trees than stars.

image.alt: Sunlight falling through tall old-growth Douglas fir trees with young trees below

probes.question: True or false: there are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.

sources.title: Crowther et al. (2015), Mapping tree density at a global scale, Nature
